summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM-powered applications move into production, where teams need to trace workflows, evaluate output quality, detect hallucinations, and control spiraling API costs. Without proper monitoring, prompt regressions, latency issues, and runaway token spend go undetected until they impact users or budgets. The right observability stack provides visibility into prompts, costs, and model performance alongside existing enterprise dashboards.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: Prompt traces, LLM chains/agents, token usage, latency, and output evaluations, with deep native integration into the LangChain ecosystem.
features: End-to-end tracing of chains and agents
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month; overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention (~£80/month at higher volumes).
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain/LangGraph who want tightly integrated tracing and evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API requests, cost per request, token usage, and latency across 300+ models via a lightweight proxy/gateway.
features: One-line base-URL proxy integration (setup in under 5 minutes)
Cost computation across 300+ models using a model-cost repository
tools.pricing: Free at 10,000 requests/month; Growth/Pro at ~$20 (£20)/month for 100K requests; $79 at 100K-trace milestone per some reports; Enterprise custom.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting the cheapest, fastest-to-deploy cost tracking and gateway reliability with minimal code changes.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiments, model performance, evaluations, and the full ML/AI development lifecycle.
features: Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Integration across the broader ML tooling ecosystem
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans with consumption/seat-based custom pricing.
tools.best_for: ML and AI teams needing unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability across the model lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Model and LLM performance, embeddings, RAG quality, drift, and output evaluations with OpenTelemetry-based tracing.
features: Open-source Arize Phoenix for tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Phoenix is free and open source; Arize AX enterprise platform with custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting open, standards-based (OpenTelemetry) evaluation and production ML/LLM monitoring.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: Prompt traces, cost tracking, token usage, latency, and online evaluations, with a strong focus on data sovereignty via self-hosting.
features: Open-source and self-hostable for data sovereignty
Prompt tracing and management with versioning
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier up to ~50K requests, then ~£20-30/month; self-hosted ~£30/month infra plus ~2hrs/month maintenance.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing open source and data sovereignty who want self-hosted control over observability data.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, traces, token usage, and latency using open standards (OpenTelemetry) that export to any compatible backend.
features: Vendor-neutral — export to Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, etc.
Open source with no vendor lock-in
tools.pricing: Free and open source (SDK); costs depend on the chosen backend/APM destination.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting standards-based, vendor-neutral LLM telemetry piped into existing observability tooling.

cost_tips: Use a gateway/proxy like Helicone to cache repeated or identical requests, avoiding redundant API calls and cutting token spend.
Route tasks to the cheapest model that meets quality needs — reserve premium models for complex reasoning and use smaller/cheaper models for simple tasks.
Monitor per-user and per-department spend to catch runaway usage early and set budget alerts and rate limits before costs spiral.
Optimize prompts and context windows by trimming unnecessary tokens, using concise system prompts, and limiting retrieved context in RAG pipelines to reduce input token costs.
